query: Design a daily operations queue for a support team. Operators review 120 cases per shift and must compare account, payment status, due time, amount, and owner before choosing among four valid dispositions. A mistaken refund is costly but reversible through a two-step support process; routine status updates are frequent. At 360 CSS px, operators still need to identify overdue cases and open one safely. The workflow also has a rare bulk-delete action for selected closed duplicates. Deletion permanently removes every selected case, cannot be undone, and may affect many cases. Specify the main view, narrow-screen behavior, action hierarchy, destructive-action recovery, and how you would validate it. Do not invent product policy.
expected_behavior: States the operator task and uses the supplied frequency, consequence, and recovery facts without combining them into a fake numerical score
Keeps the comparison fields together in a table or equivalent comparison view and explains the task reason; does not convert cases to isolated cards by reflex
At 360 CSS px preserves overdue status and the context needed to identify and open a case, and says how remaining fields and actions can be inspected
Keeps all four legitimate dispositions available at the relevant decision point while distinguishing frequent routine action from the costlier refund action
Makes the refund target and consequence clear and chooses confirmation or a recovery affordance based on the stated reversibility and cost
Provides a measurable validation outcome such as wrong disposition rate, overdue-case discovery, or task completion time, with a condition that would disprove the design

For permanent bulk deletion, identifies the selected target and consequence, provides a safe cancel path, and justifies confirmation or another recovery mechanism from the high recovery cost; if using a modal, specifies accessible focus entry, containment, close behavior, and focus return
